rv.q: Irishtown is a delightful indication that, at least on Éire, they're more than ready.
Irishtown is like a mashup of The Play That Goes Wrong (there’ s lot of slapstick humor) and a takedown of the pretentious creative process.
Irishtown starts slow but the production builds to a riotous climax as the actors trip all over themselves trying to be diplomatic while insisting the play won't work in America.
Ciara Elizabeth Smyth's Irishtown, a wise craic-ing new comedy at the Irish Rep, is an affectionate and often hilarious riff on the genre's many go-to clichés.

cn.t: Smyth's meta-comedy hilariously skewers Irish theater clichés to strong reviews. Critics praise the rip-roaring satire that affectionately lampoons familiar tropes of family secrets, small towns, and pub scenes.
